Marco (AE): Heads up — Sylph legal just pushed back on the POC. Main asks: BYO-KMS proof, SSO configuration docs, and network egress details. Can we get a quick unblock?
Talia (SE): Got it. Which KMS model do they expect? Customer is asking about HSM-backed keys vs cloud KMS.
Marco (AE): They're CISO-level paranoid — they explicitly asked for HSM attestation + ability to audit key usage. Also want an SSO assertion flow diagram.
James (Infra Eng): We can produce a KMS integration plan. For BYO-KMS we generally support the following flow:
```
1) Customer provisions key in their KMS (AWS KMS / CloudHSM / Azure KeyVault)
2) Mutual TLS + IAM policy for key access
3) Redwood side uses wrapped DEKs, no persistent plaintext keys
```
James (Infra Eng): For HSM attestation we'll need time. Might require engagement with infra team and security to create an audit artifact. Estimated 3-5 business days for a concrete doc.
Sara (CISO): We need to confirm what level of attestation they want (e.g., FIPS 140-2 Level 2 vs Level 3). Also need their questionnaire responses for vendor risk. Please attach their questionnaire and any prior answers.
Marco (AE): Sending the questionnaire now. Attaching highlights: Q12: "Do you permit BYO-KMS with customer-managed keys?" Q19: "Can you provide cryptographic attestation?" Q27: "SSO: support for SAML 2.0 or OIDC?"
Marco (AE): (uploads) sylph_vdr_security_qs.pdf :eyes:
Talia (SE): Quick ask for James: can we produce an SSO diagram that shows SP <-> IdP, assertion flow, and token lifetimes? Sylph wants token TTLs and refresh behaviour documented.
James (Infra Eng): Yes. I can sketch that and include sample config snippets for SAML metadata and OIDC client settings. Will need to know whether they expect IdP-initiated or SP-initiated flows.
Marco (AE): Sylph prefers SP-initiated for session control, but they'll accept both.
Priya (VP Sales): This is an exec-level blocker. Marco — can we get an internal exec bridge if CISO still isn't satisfied after docs? I want to be ready to escalate tomorrow if needed.
Sara (CISO): If we produce the attestation and a short runbook for key rotation/audit logs, that should cover most enterprise asks. For anything beyond that, we should have a security SME on the bridge.
Talia (SE): I'll draft the SSO diagram + sample config by EOD tomorrow. James — can you slot a 30-min working session with infra to draft the KMS attestation artifact?
James (Infra Eng): Sure. I can do a quick sync at 10:00am PT tomorrow. Adding action: create attestation outline + sample policy.
Marco (AE): I'll coordinate and send Sylph a timeline: docs by EOD tomorrow, attestation draft in 48-72 hours. Also asking for their preferred bridge time if they want exec escalation.
Priya (VP Sales): Make the ask explicit: "If we can deliver docs + attestation draft within 72 hours, will CISO accept that as a path to continue the POC?" We need a yes/no from them.
Marco (AE): Sending that wording to Sylph now.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: docs/sales/presales/sylph_poc/ssoconfig_v1.md created by Talia at 2026-03-21T18:12:10Z
Marco (AE): Sylph responded: they can accept the 72-hour attestation draft as long as there's a firm exec bridge scheduled *if* any gaps remain. They proposed Tue 3pm PT for an exec call.
Sara (CISO): I can join Tue 3pm PT. Priya?
Priya (VP Sales): I'll be there for the first 15 minutes to support. Good job moving fast.
Talia (SE): Noted — I'll finalize SSO config doc and add a short section on token TTLs and refresh flow.
James (Infra Eng): Blocking ask for infra: access to our attestation template and someone to sign off on the audit logs format. I'll ping eng-security offline.
Marco (AE): Closing loop here — bridge scheduled Tue 3pm PT, deliverables: SSO diagram + config (Talia) by EOD tomorrow, KMS attestation draft (James) in 72 hours, Sylph to confirm acceptance once docs delivered.
Priya (VP Sales): Thanks team. If bridge still shows material gaps, escalate to execs and legal. :thumbsup:
Marco (AE): Thanks — will keep thread updated with any changes.
